method: Every package in build/packages/ was classified. Removal candidates were required to have no dependent required feature, verified with rpm -q --whatrequires inside the built image rather than by reading the package lists.

removals.whyPresent: Arrives in the quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc:44 base image. It is not in any consumer package set; build/packages/developer.txt lists it deliberately for the developer profile only.
removals.rationale: 12.6 MB Go binary providing an interactive container workflow that a consumer Bunny OS installation has no use for. rpm -q --whatrequires toolbox returns nothing, so no required feature depends on it. Removed to reduce executable surface, not to reduce a scan score - the scan count did not move.

measuredEffect.note: The removal is real at the filesystem and rpmdb level and changed no scan number, which is the honest result and the reason 'reduce the scan count' is a prohibited motive. See docs/PACKAGE_MINIMISATION.md for why the SBOM is unchanged.

retained.reason: rpm -q --whatrequires podman returns bootc. bootc is the update mechanism; removing podman removes the ability to update the system. podman is also listed in build/packages/installer.txt. It carries 6 of the 24 blocking Critical/High findings and still cannot be removed.
rpm -q --whatrequires skopeo returns bootc and rpm-ostree. Same argument as podman.
Screen reader. Protected: removing it would make the system unusable for blind users, which is not a trade a scan score can justify.
Accessibility bus. Every assistive technology depends on it.
Pointer accessibility. Protected for the same reason as orca.
Required to unlock an encrypted installation, including from recovery media. Removing it would strand users out of their own data.
Wi-Fi, graphics and storage controllers need it. Removing it to shrink the image would break hardware support on the machines the project has not yet tested.
Firmware updates, including security fixes delivered outside the OS.
Mandatory access control. It is part of the mitigation argument for every unresolved container-stack finding.
Drops unsolicited inbound traffic by default.
Sandboxing for Flatpak applications and the plugin boundary.
Diagnostic available without network access, on media a user boots when the installed system will not start.
